Package neqsim.process.processmodel

Class AutoRecycleBuilder

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.processmodel.AutoRecycleBuilder
public final class AutoRecycleBuilder extends Object
Finds feedback loops in a flowsheet and closes them with explicit Recycle tear streams.

A loop that is left as an implicit tear (a stream wired straight back into an upstream mixer) has no convergence criterion of its own: only the outer sweep can close it, with no acceleration and no per-tear tolerance. This class locates such loops - inside a ProcessSystem through strongly connected components of its ProcessGraph, and across the areas of a ProcessModel through streams that flow from a later area back into an earlier one - and rewires each one through a seeded tear stream plus a Recycle.

Only inlets that can be rewired are torn: MixerInterface and Manifold expose replaceStream(int, StreamInterface). A loop that closes on any other equipment type is reported and left untouched rather than silently mis-wired.

Version:
1.0
Author:
NeqSim

  • Method Details

    • insertRecycles

      public static List<Recycle> insertRecycles(ProcessSystem process, double tolerance)
      Inserts recycles on every feedback loop inside one process system that has none.

      One edge is torn per round and the loop structure is recomputed afterwards, so an area containing several nested cycles gets exactly the tears it needs and no more - every extra tear is another sub-iteration at run time.

      Parameters:
      process - the flowsheet to rewire; ignored when null
      tolerance - relative tear tolerance passed to Recycle.setTolerance(double), must be positive
      Returns:
      the recycles created, empty when the flowsheet already closes every loop

    • insertRecycles

      public static List<Recycle> insertRecycles(ProcessModel model, double tolerance)
      Inserts recycles on cross-area feedback streams and then on every loop inside each area.

      A stream produced by an area that runs after its consumer is a tear of the outer Gauss-Seidel sweep. Each one is replaced by a seeded tear stream in the consumer and a Recycle registered in the producing area, so the loop gets its own convergence criterion and acceleration.

      Parameters:
      model - the multi-area model to rewire; ignored when null
      tolerance - relative tear tolerance passed to Recycle.setTolerance(double), must be positive
      Returns:
      the recycles created, empty when the model already closes every loop

    • selectTearEdge

      private static ProcessEdge selectTearEdge(List<ProcessNode> loop)
      Picks the material edge inside a loop that is cheapest to tear.

      Candidates are limited to edges that end on a rewireable inlet. The one with the smallest recycle ratio - tear flow divided by the total flow into the consuming unit - is chosen, because the convergence rate of a direct-substitution tear is governed by that ratio: a small side stream entering a large mixer contracts in a few passes, while tearing the main line makes the loop iterate on its own throughput.

      Parameters:
      loop - the strongly connected component to tear
      Returns:
      the selected edge, or null when no edge in the loop can be rewired

    • recycleRatio

      private static double recycleRatio(ProcessEdge edge)

    • tuneRecycle

      private static void tuneRecycle(ProcessSystem owner, Recycle recycle, double tolerance)
      Configures a generated recycle for fast and stable convergence.

      The loop starts on direct substitution, which is the robust choice while the tear is still far from its fixed point, and adaptive acceleration lets it switch itself to Wegstein once its flow error stops contracting - that is exactly the oscillating low-flow loop that otherwise iterates to the budget. An absolute flow tolerance scaled to the largest flow in the owning area is added as well, so a tear on a near-zero leg converges on its absolute change rather than on a relative error that stays at order one.

      Parameters:
      owner - the process system that owns the recycle, used for the flow scale
      recycle - the recycle to configure
      tolerance - relative tear tolerance
